- Sustained throughput: average 300 req/s, peak 600 req/s for short bursts (5–10 minutes).
- Concurrency per tenant: up to 75 concurrent sessions; many sessions will be streaming websocket flows with long-lived connections (avg session 6 minutes).

Kim / Marcus / Sofia — quick engineering notes ahead of the deep-dive. Copying the key asks from Sofia above for context.

Quoted for context:
> - Latency targets (p95): US <= 150 ms, EU <= 200 ms, APAC <= 300 ms.
> - Sustained throughput: average 300 req/s, peak 600 req/s for short bursts (5–10 minutes).
> - Concurrency per tenant: up to 75 concurrent sessions; many sessions will be streaming websocket flows with long-lived connections (avg session 6 minutes).

Clarifying questions / notes:
- Streaming: our websocket path keeps per-stream KV caches and supports ~60 tokens/s, but tail p95 depends on per-stream batching and batching window. For strict p95 we recommend disabling cross-stream batching for pinned (EU) traffic. That will increase cost but keeps latency bounded.
- Token sizes: we need avg/max tokens per request. If avg request is small (<120 tokens) we can meet your targets more easily; if many requests approach ~1k tokens, we will need larger GPU memory or quantized variants which change latency profile.
- Concurrency model: 75 concurrent websocket sessions for a tenant is fine if pinned to a dedicated pool. We should size the pool to allow 1.5x headroom on concurrency to avoid queueing.
- Throughput bursts: autoscaling handles burst to 600 req/s, but 5–10m sustained bursts at that level require reserved burst capacity on Dedicated. Otherwise we may see transient p95 spikes.
- Observability: we can stream per-tenant traces and token-level latency histograms into your EU logging sink (if configured). Need to confirm log retention policy (how long you want telemetry retained in EU).

Proposed defaults for the pilot sizing doc (we’ll refine on the call):
- EU pool: reserve for 100 concurrent sessions, headroom for 150.
- US pool: reserve for 150 concurrent, headroom for 225.
- APAC pool: minimal validation pool with 25 concurrent.

I’ll prepare a short slide with latency expectations vs token-size and whether quantized models are needed for meeting the p95 in APAC.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Marcus on the sizing and bring the pilot runbook to the deep-dive.

-Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
